findings:
The revised plan resolves all 15 findings from the first review, and the reviewer checked each fix against the code: player missiles and enemy rockets now destroy each other, the player takes damage only from a rocket's blast, rockets can no longer be overrun by their own launcher, a ward's own brain can refuse an escort tow during a telegraphed attack, and the test-time budget is split per task, with the time-freeing task first. No blocking problem is left. Eight minor gaps remain, all fixable inside their own tasks without changing the design. The agents that build each task do not see this review, so I recommend writing findings 1–4 into the plan or into the task descriptions when you approve.

| # | Severity | Problem | Fix | Tasks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | minor | An ally fighter's contact hitbox is on the player-weapon layer, so a rocket touching an ally pops harmlessly about half the time. | The rocket's shoot-down handler reacts only to projectile hitboxes, not ship contact boxes, and a test with a real ally fighter covers it. | t5 |
| 2 | minor | The Assault dodge and Warhead-escape tests assume Open Space speeds (420/700 px/s), but the base Assault fighter moves at 360 px/s. | Take each mode's test speeds from that mode's real player, and state the Assault counterplay: stay out of the trigger radius or shoot the warhead. | t5, t6 |
| 3 | minor | At its orbit radius the corvette is outside the Assault view about 40% of the time, so it can telegraph and fire unseen. | In Assault a salvo starts only while the corvette is inside the camera view; add a test, make t8 depend on t4, and add the view-rect section to t8. | t8, t17 |
| 4 | minor | Cluster rockets need 700 px of range, but the Assault hold radius tops out at about 540, so Assault almost never sees one. | Give Assault its own range for choosing a Cluster salvo (with a test), or record that Assault has no Cluster salvos. | t8 |
| 5 | minor | The cyan shield arc is drawn on an armoured Ram even though it is not taking the hits, so players will credit it with deflections. | Draw the shield dormant or hide it while the host is armoured; add a unit test. | t2, t12 |
| 6 | minor | Per-task time allowances of 0.5–2 s are smaller than the suite's normal run-to-run variation, so they cannot be checked. | The time script reports each task's own new test files and checks the allowance against those; the whole-suite total is checked only against the ceiling. | t1 |
| 7 | minor | A rail faster than a rocket's cruise speed could still let a corvette catch its own armed rocket (nothing puts a corvette on such a rail today). | Never let a rocket slow below 1.1× its inherited speed, or have the rail fallback fire sideways. | t7 |
| 8 | minor | One Assault corvette range test passes comfortably only if the starting range drift is near zero. | Seed the brain so the start is fixed, and never loosen the bound. | t8 |

**1.** `ally_fighter.tscn:57` puts the ally's contact hitbox on layer 64, which is also the player-weapon layer. Rockets resolve a shoot-down in their HurtBox handler, and Godot orders the two areas' callbacks arbitrarily. Allies appear in deep_space, the same section that gains corvettes in t17.

**2.** The "both modes" rows for dodging rockets and escaping a triggered warhead use 420/700 px/s stubs. Assault only reaches 700+ with the unlockable engine-boost module.

**3.** The 460 px orbit, set against the Assault view's half-height, puts the corvette above or below the screen on a large share of its orbit, so a player would never see the telegraph the design promises.

**4.** The Cluster salvo needs at least 700 px, but in Assault the hold radius is clamped to about 540 px. Without a separate Assault range, the Cluster Rocket is effectively Open-Space-only.

**5.** The absorber correctly refuses hits the armoured host deflects (round-1 finding 9), but the arc is still drawn at full strength.

**6.** These allowances are below measurement noise. The 240 s ceiling stays the real limit.

**7.** This is not reachable today. It is worth a one-line clamp now, while the rocket code is being written.

**8.** The bounded-chase row's margin depends on the brain's initial drift phase. Make the start deterministic rather than widening the tolerance.

Full evidence, including the resolution table for every round-1 finding, is in 4-review.md under Round 2.
